title: Slot prewarmer and deferred KV eviction: refactor scheduler + dependency upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: The serving runtime experiences periodic tail-latency spikes under OLTP-like workloads. Investigation shows two recurring sources of contention: (1) scheduler hotspots during slot allocation and cold-start of execution slots, and (2) synchronous KV cache evictions that block the read path. This ticket refactors the scheduler prewarming and introduces a deferred eviction pipeline for KV cache to reduce blocking. The goal is to simplify the commit path, lower 95th/99th token latency by ~20% in mixed small/long seq workloads, and make the runtime less sensitive to short bursts without changing external APIs.
design_notes:
- Implement a slot prewarmer that maintains a small pool of ready worker slots per shard; prewarmer uses background leasing with backoff and health checks.
- Replace global eviction path with per-shard deferred eviction queue processed by a low-priority background worker to avoid blocking hot reads.
- Introduce per-shard lease tokens to avoid a global lock during allocation and lease migration.
- Add metrics: prewarm_pool_size, deferred_eviction_queue_depth, eviction_latency_seconds_bucket, slot_acquire_latency_ms.
- Short-circuit path: if prewarm pool is empty, fast-create path remains but is throttled to protect allocator under overload.
- Dependency upgrades: bump tokio to 1.15 and bump protobuf/prost to latest minor to pick up async improvements and avoid past incompatibilities with our kernel dispatcher.
- Trade-offs: slightly increased steady-state memory (small pool) vs. lower tail latency; deferred eviction may delay reclaim by up to 500ms which we accept for most production workloads but will make threshold tunable per-tenant.
acceptance_criteria: 95th token latency improvement >= 15% on mixed workload benchmark (internal perf-runner).
99th token latency improvement >= 10% or absolute 99th <= 120ms for target model+seq distribution.
No increase in per-token cost >2% when running production traffic profile.
Automated unit tests for lease tokens, prewarmer lifecycle, and deferred eviction behaviors added and passing.
Canary rollout plan documented and validated: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with rollback triggers based on latency or error budget breach.
comments: 2025-11-06 - Triaged: found correlation between slot allocation spike and NVidia driver stalls reported in infra logs. Assigned to Mateo for initial spike repros.

2025-11-18 - Prototype: Mateo pushed an experiment that creates a tiny prewarm pool per shard behind a feature flag; bench shows 12% drop in 95th on small-seq workload (internal run id: perf/2025-11-18/slot-prewarm). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6478

2025-12-02 - Design review: PM (Liu Chen) prefers per-tenant tunables to avoid memory blowup for high-tenant-count clusters; security reviewed deferred eviction for side-channel concerns and signed off.

2025-12-14 - Dependency work: upgraded tokio to 1.15 in a fork branch; hit a regression with blocking threads in the scheduler test harness. Root cause: older blocking-thread pool assumptions in our custom runtime. Created followup ENG-33145 to align blocking pool sizing.

2026-01-04 - Perf lab: full-suite A/B run (canary vs baseline) shows 18% 95th reduction on mixed workload, 22% on small-seq-heavy. Observed a 0.8% CPU increase and ~1.3% memory increase for prewarm pools. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/perf/dashboards/slot-prewarm-2026-01-04

2026-01-12 - Code review: PRs split into three parts: prewarmer core + metrics (PR #6521), deferred-eviction queue + tests (PR #6523), tokio/prost upgrade + CI fixes (PR #6527). Requesting owners: @core-runtime, @kvcache. Blocking: finalize graceful shutdown ordering for prewarmer to avoid double-leases during restart.

2026-01-18 - Rollout plan finalized: start with internal infra-only tenants (non-customer) for 1% traffic, monitor eviction queue depth and slot_acquire_latency_ms; rollback if 99th latency regresses >5% for 15m. Added canary automation task in console for runtime-1.20 release.
notes_for_oncall: If tails regress after rollout, toggle feature-flag:runtime.prewarm.enabled=false and inspect deferred_eviction_queue_depth and slot_acquire_latency_ms. If eviction queue grows > 10k for >10m, temporarily increase eviction worker concurrency and apply emergency compaction.
